public_body: Ashland School District Reorganization Task Force
overall: The AG found the superintendent-created Ashland School District Reorganization Task Force was a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law and violated it by not posting notice, not certifying member review, and keeping deficient minutes; it ordered compliance and minute amendments.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the task force failed to post notice of its meetings, which it held without publicly posting agendas.
allegations.key_passage: Indeed, the Task Force did not post notice of its meetings, and we find that its failure to do so violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged task force members did not complete the required certification that they reviewed the Open Meeting Law, its regulations, and the AG's guide.
allegations.key_passage: It is clear that the Task Force members did not complete this step because its members did not believe that they were subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the task force failed to keep proper minutes; the minutes omitted meeting place and detail on disagreement or substantive discussion.
allegations.key_passage: The minutes do not state the place of the meetings and do not state in detail whether there was disagreement or substantive discussion on any topic.

allegations.summary: Task force contended it was not a public body because the superintendent created it under the Connelly exception; the AG rejected this and found it subject to the law.
allegations.key_passage: The Task Force therefore satisfies all three factors, and we conclude that the Task Force is a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint named the superintendent and school committee as violators; the superintendent as an individual official was found not to be a public body.
allegations.key_passage: The Superintendent, an individual public official, is not a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law, and he therefore could not have violated it.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements by the Task Force, extending to any public bodies the School Committee establishes in the future.

Amend the Task Force's meeting minutes to include the required details to the best of its ability, using all available means including attendees' memories and individual notations, within 90 days of receipt of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Task Force's immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.

source.publisher_filename: DETERMINATION - 9 1 2016 - OML 2016-116 - ASHLAND SCHOOL DISTRICT REORGANIZATION TASK FORCE.pdf

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
